# ChassisDeliver-150 Dataset License and Use Terms

Version: anonymous-review draft 1.0

This notice applies to the ChassisDeliver-150 benchmark materials in
`benchmark/chassisdeliver150/` and the resolved benchmark label files in
`code/chassisgate/data/benchmark/`.

It does not grant rights in third-party resources referenced by the benchmark,
including PubMed records, external database entries, KEGG/BiGG/BioModels
resources, DrugCLIP assets, or GEM model files.

## Anonymous Review Use

During double-blind review, reviewers may use this dataset only for evaluating,
reproducing, and verifying the accompanying anonymous paper submission.

Before the authors publish a formal de-anonymized release, do not:

- redistribute this dataset or a renamed copy;
- upload it to a public benchmark hub, package registry, repository, or model
  leaderboard;
- use it in a separate paper, preprint, report, product, service, or benchmark
  claim without citing the original ChassisDeliver-150 work;
- remove or obscure this notice, the citation file, or the checksum record.

## Attribution Requirement

Any permitted use must identify the benchmark as:

> ChassisDeliver-150: a chassis-conditioned biosynthetic deliverability
> benchmark for molecule-chassis pairs.

For anonymous review, cite the accompanying anonymous BIBM submission. After
de-anonymized release, cite the public paper and dataset DOI listed in
`CITATION.cff`.

## No Ownership Transfer

Access to this review artifact does not transfer ownership of the benchmark,
its evidence-card compilation, its annotation protocol, or its resolved labels.

Derived datasets, label conversions, cleaned copies, and renamed mirrors that
substantially reuse ChassisDeliver-150 must preserve attribution to the original
benchmark and must not imply independent creation.

## Warranty

The dataset is provided for research review and reproducibility. It is provided
as-is, without warranty of fitness for any particular purpose.

## Public Release Placeholder

The public release license should be finalized after review. Reasonable options
include a standard Creative Commons license for the dataset plus a separate
software license for code, or a custom academic-use license if redistribution
must remain restricted.
